source.title: Transformers Learn Low Sensitivity Functions: Investigations and Implications
source.authors: Bhavya Vasudeva; Deqing Fu; Tianyi Zhou; Elliott Kau; Youqi Huang; Vatsal Sharan

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking training dynamics on modular addition using sensitivity as a different progress measure; it does not reproduce the original mechanistic measurements.
record.gate_note: The main grokking experiment reports train/test accuracy, sensitivity, and weight norm over training. The appendix also reports sparse-parity learning, where train and test accuracy reach 100% together; that is a related algorithmic-task result but not an overfit-then-delayed-generalization experiment, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: It trains a one-layer Transformer on a + b mod 113 and reports train and test accuracy over training. Train accuracy saturates while test accuracy stays low (epochs 500–9,800), then the model groks, which bears on V1. It also tracks a new continuous measure, input sensitivity, that changes before the jump, which bears on V2. It uses a different measure from the originals' mechanistic ones, hence T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that sensitivity is a progress measure for grokking on modular addition. It decreases while training loss and test accuracy are flat, and it marks stages paralleling Nanda et al.'s phases. They add an extra 'noise reduction' phase after grokking that they say other mechanistic measures miss. They also say weight norm is not a progress measure in the 3,000–9,800 interval.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a modular-addition grokking task and training dynamics, but measures input sensitivity with Gaussian noise rather than the mechanistic interpretability measures discussed in the cited grokking work; model and optimization details for this experiment are not stated in the provided text.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer transformers on sparse parity (d=40, p=4; six settings): sensitivity rises while train and test accuracy sit near 50%. It then converges to 0.1 as both reach 100% together. There is no overfit-then-generalize gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity changes before accuracy rises when transformers learn sparse parities (hidden progress without a grokking delay).

record.problems: The grokking result is a single modular-addition task and model; the text provides no numerical accuracy values or uncertainty estimates for that result, and the post-9,800 accuracy is shown only in figures. The proposed circuit interpretation is not directly tested in this experiment.
record.rows_left_out: Sparse-parity training dynamics are recorded as an aggregate finding in fits_no_version rather than as a grokking row: the appendix describes them as a separate progress-measure experiment and does not report an overfit-then-delayed-generalization event.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size; other algorithmic tasks; numeric accuracy values; seeds or uncertainty.
Identification of the Fourier circuit; whether memorizing components are removed; any causal test. Sensitivity phases are mapped onto Nanda et al.'s phases by interpretation only.
Entirely untested in the grokking experiment.
Entirely untested. Weight decay is mentioned but not varied, and there is no critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Entirely untested. The optimizer and numerical settings of the grokking run are not even reported.

missing.what: Weight norm falls dramatically during epochs 500–3,000 (the circuit-formation phase), unlike its flat curve during 3,000–9,800.
Training details of the grokking run (training fraction, optimizer, weight decay value, seeds) are not reported anywhere in the text. Researchers comparing V1/V5/V7 settings need these.

record.verdict_notes: Fix the dangling R10 reference in fits_no_version: there is no R10 row, and the sparse-parity result is an aggregate finding, so row_ids are left empty. I dropped the reader's V2 limits_scope label built on R9: a flat weight norm in one interval does not qualify V2 when another continuous measure anticipates the jump, and the norm falls in the earlier phase. Sensitivity is non-monotonic over training (down, up, down, up/down), so its phase mapping rests on the authors' interpretation. The study is a single unreplicated run with figure-only accuracy values and no uncertainty. The rest of the paper (sensitivity across architectures, robustness, flatness) does not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment uses one modular-addition setting; it does not vary training-set size or test whether smaller training sets require more optimization.
Sensitivity is measured as a progress signal, but the study does not identify or causally test the generalizing circuit or remove memorizing components.
Non-algorithmic datasets and initialization-scale or weight-norm switches are not tested as causes of grokking-like delays.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested for delayed generalization.
The study does not test an efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below a threshold.
The study does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts as explanations of the delay.

rows.subject: one-layer Transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Measured sensitivity by adding random Gaussian noise to number embeddings.
rows.value: Sensitivity values continue to decrease smoothly while training loss does not reduce.
rows.note: The authors present the decreasing sensitivity as a progress measure during the period when accuracy remains low.

source_check.locator_found: Section 7.3, Figure 8 discussion: sensitivity decreases smoothly from epoch 3000 while loss remains unchanged; Gaussian noise σ = 0.1.

rows.subject: one-layer Transformer model
rows.value: Sensitivity drops significantly while training accuracy saturates to 100 and test accuracy increases but cannot saturate.
rows.note: The authors describe this as the memorization phase.
rows.check: Memorization-phase sensitivity (epochs 0–500) comes before the plateau. It says nothing about whether a progress measure anticipates the later jump; 'partial' has no basis against V2.

rows.subject: one-layer Transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Measured sensitivity during the stated circuit-formation phase.
rows.value: Sensitivity goes up again while test accuracy remains low and flat.
rows.note: The authors say the fall in weight norms suggests circuit formation likely happens due to weight decay; they do not directly identify the circuit here.
rows.check: Sensitivity rises during epochs 500–3,000. Linking this to circuit formation is the authors' interpretation; no circuit is measured. It cannot show gradual circuit formation. It does show the measure is non-monotonic.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix A.5, Circuit Formation paragraph: epochs 500–3,000.

rows.subject: one-layer Transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Measured sensitivity during the stated cleanup phase.
rows.value: Sensitivity starts to decrease; the authors interpret this as progress toward using Fourier features.
rows.note: The interpretation of Fourier-feature use is the authors’ account; this experiment does not independently establish circuit formation or component removal.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix A.5, Clean up paragraph: epochs 3,000–9,800; Section 7.3.

rows.subject: one-layer Transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Measured sensitivity after the grokked phase.
rows.value: Sensitivity has an upward and then downward trend.
rows.note: The authors attribute the trend to further Fourier noise reduction and describe the Fourier basis as becoming more robust.
rows.check: Post-grokking sensitivity (epoch 9,800 onwards) is after the jump, so it cannot bear on whether progress measures anticipate it. The noise-reduction account is the authors' interpretation.

rows.subject: one-layer Transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Compared weight norm over training with sensitivity and test accuracy.
rows.value: Weight norm has the same flat curve as test accuracy during this interval.
rows.note: This is the study’s comparator for the sensitivity progress measure.
rows.check: Weight norm is flat during epochs 3,000–9,800 but falls dramatically during 500–3,000 (Appendix A.5). One flat interval for one candidate measure does not show V2's effect absent, so 'absent' overstates it. The row also omits the earlier fall.

source_check.locator_found: Section 7.3, final sentence of first paragraph: weight norm and test accuracy are flat during epochs 3,000–9,800.
